#+title: Task: Add a product short code to trade type

This page documents a [[id:31C868B9-306E-4282-BA8C-07E647021B34][task]] in the [[id:688959F0-A1AB-4021-A57E-1103AD92773A][Redesign ores.trading on data-oriented principles]] story. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance, and any notes or results.

* Goal

=trade_type= carries =code=, which holds ORE's =TradeType= string:
=Bond=, =BondTRS=, =EquityAutoDeltaHedgedOption=. Those values are
ORE's, they are long, and a trader cannot key them quickly.

=counterparty= already holds the pattern this task wants. Its
=short_code= is a natural key, described in the model as "a brief
mnemonic code used in trading systems", and it sits beside
=full_name=.

This task gives =trade_type= the same treatment: a short mnemonic
code of three to six characters, distinct from ORE's =code=, minted
once for each of the 119 product types.

It also corrects a claim the documentation already makes. The
identifiers table on each of the 88 product knowledge pages carries a
row labelled "ORE Studio product code" whose value is ORE's
=TradeType= code. No ORE Studio product code exists yet, so that
label names something the model does not hold.

* Acceptance

- =trade_type= carries a =short_code= column, marked =natural_key=,
  following the =counterparty.short_code= precedent.
- Every one of the 119 rows in
  =trading_trade_types_populate.sql= carries a short code of three to
  six characters.
- Short codes are unique across the catalogue, and a uniqueness
  constraint enforces it rather than convention.
- The identifiers table on every product knowledge page states the
  short code under a label that matches what the model holds, and the
  row naming ORE's own code says so.
- [[id:C5C95B29-2EF9-4DFC-9E04-428C41C1925D][ORE Products by Asset Class]] carries the short code alongside the ORE
  code, so the two can be read against each other.

* Plan

(Implementation strategy. Written when work starts; key decisions
are distilled into the parent story's =* Decisions= at close, but the
plan itself stays — it is the historical record of what we did.)

* Notes

Open questions for the plan.

- Whether the short code is allocated by hand per product or derived
  from the ORE code by a rule. A rule is reproducible, but it will
  collide: =EquityForwardVolatilityAgreement= and
  =FxForwardVolatilityAgreement= share most of their words.
- Whether the short code or ORE's =code= is the primary key. ORE's
  =code= is the primary key today and the wire format depends on it,
  so the short code is most likely a second natural key rather than a
  replacement.
- Whether =Failed= needs a short code. It is ORE's marker for a trade
  it could not build and the product catalogue excludes it, so it
  probably does not.
